drivers: Record copper output ~890K tonnes (2025) — strong export earnings
Record maize harvest >4M tonnes — reduced food import needs
Debt restructuring ~94% complete — sovereign risk premium collapsing
IMF ECF programme completed (final US$190M disbursement) — successor programme talks next
MPR held at 13.25% at the August 2026 MPC (26 Aug) — lowest since mid-2024; attractive real yields still support carry inflows
Yuan mining tax corridor reducing USD demand
Gross international reserves at historic high of US$5.5 billion
Swearing-in of President Hichilema and Vice-President for a second term held 1 Sep 2026 (public holiday) — policy continuity now formalised
BoZ cut statutory reserve requirements (early Aug 2026) — supportive of bank liquidity
Seasonal import demand and month-end FX demand pressuring the kwacha in mid-September
trendAnalysis.outlook: Kwacha softer into 15 Sep: USD/ZMW mid ~19.42 (open.er-api.com), vs ~19.20 on 12 Sep and ~18.83 a month ago — pushing toward the top of the broad 18.40–19.50 consolidation band on renewed import/market demand. The official/parallel premium remains narrow (~+1.84%), signalling no acute FX scarcity. With re-election formalised at the 1 Sep ceremony and the MPC holding at 13.25% on 26 August, focus shifts to the make-up of the new economic team and the 2027 budget.
trendAnalysis.projection3m: USD/ZMW 18.50–19.80 range. Post-election policy continuity supportive; import demand and copper-price swings the main risks.
trendAnalysis.projection6m: USD/ZMW 18.00–20.00 range. Direction hinges on fiscal continuity and copper earnings.
